relevance: Governs how long someone has to file a lawsuit after a legal wrong occurs. This applies ACROSS every document type in your knowledge base (rental, employment, consumer, property) — it's the answer to 'can I still do something about this?' which is one of the most common real questions a user will ask in the chat/Q&A feature, regardless of which specific document they uploaded.

sections.title: Limitation period for breach of contract
sections.text: A suit for compensation for the breach of any contract (not otherwise specifically covered elsewhere in the Act) must be filed within 3 years. The 3-year clock starts when the contract is broken — or, if there were successive breaches, from the date of the most recent breach — or, for a continuing breach, from the date the breach ceased (a fresh limitation period restarts at every moment a continuing breach continues, per Section 22).
sections.typical_clause_conflict: This is the DEFAULT time limit — directly relevant to flagging Indian Contract Act Section 28 violations (clauses that try to impose a shorter time limit than this statutory default, e.g. 'any claim must be raised within 7 days', are themselves void under Section 28).

sections.title: Residual limitation period
sections.text: For any suit where no other specific limitation period is prescribed elsewhere in the Act's schedule, the limitation period is 3 years from when the right to sue first arises (accrues).
sections.typical_clause_conflict: The fallback rule for document-related disputes not squarely covered by Article 55 or another specific provision — generally lands at the same 3-year answer as Article 55 for contract-adjacent claims.

sections.title: Bar of limitation
sections.text: Every suit, appeal, or application filed after the prescribed limitation period must be dismissed, even if the defendant does not specifically raise the limitation defence — the court applies this rule on its own.
sections.typical_clause_conflict: Background rule explaining WHY hitting the deadline matters so much — it's not just a technicality the other side has to raise, courts enforce it automatically.

notes_for_build_team: For the chat/Q&A feature, this Act is the right source whenever a user asks some version of 'is it too late for me to do anything?' — combine the relevant document's facts (when did the breach happen) with Article 55's 3-year rule to give a concrete, dated answer, similar to the NI Act deadline-calculator idea. This is one of the highest-leverage sections in your whole knowledge base precisely because it applies to every document type, not just one persona.
